newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK BLUE CHIPS CLOSE HIGHER, SAX UP 3.45 PTS.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK BLUE CHIPS CLOSE HIGHER, SAX UP 3.45 PTS.

text.p: Slovak blue chips closed mostly higher in thiner trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, pushing the SAX index up 3.45 points to 167.43.
Brokers said the market was led mostly by gains VSZ steel shares, which closed four crowns higher than Friday at 480.
VSZ's average price -- used in calculating the index -- rose 10.71 crowns, but brokers said the price was kept artificialy high and did not reflect the stock's real value.
One trade for VSZ was as high as 530 crowns on Monday.
"There is interest in purchasing VSZ shares, but the orders are at about 480 crowns," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.
Sykora said he did not expect significant moves of the market in either direction in near future.

"It is not yet clear whether prices have fallen enough to attract foreign investors, but we don't expect significant moves by the beginning of the Christmas holiday season, which should start within some three weeks," he said.
Oil and gas storage firm Nafta closed up 10 crowns at 1,360, but on only six shares traded.

Refiner Slovnaft was unchanged at 710 crowns. Brokers said Slovnaft's inability to move back to previous levels of above 900 crowns was due to the general bearish mood on the market and the attempts of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development to sell its stake in the refiner back to the state.

Overall volume fell to 126,530 shares, matched mostly in direct trades, from 205,039 traded on Friday. The turnover decreased to 38.38 million crowns, from 60.03 million on Friday. -- Peter Laca, Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-563-3687
